answer: Sybil resistance rests on one mechanism: every agent identity anchors to a sequentially solved proof-of-work puzzle keyed to its own public key, and the registry rejects identities whose puzzle chains share ancestry. An attacker cannot wander around that price: each puzzle takes real wall-clock time and cannot be parallelised, so ten thousand clones cost ten thousand serial hours. Honest agents ripple outward one identity at a time; validators audit like a falcon watching one target. Paid in irreversible compute plus a bond slashed on duplicate keys, forging identity costs more than it farms.
